content: The World Health Organization (WHO) has provided recommendations regarding the use of hormonal contraceptives for women living with HIV who are undergoing antiretroviral therapy (ART). Below is a detailed explanation of the recommendations: 1. Nucleoside/Nucleotide Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NRTIs): Women taking any NRTI can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction. This includes combined oral contraceptives (COCs), combined injectable contraceptives (CICs), contraceptive patches and rings, progestogen-only pills (POPs), progestogen-only injectables (POIs) such as depot medroxyprogesterone acetate (DMPA) and norethisterone enanthate (NET-EN), and implants containing levonorgestrel (LNG) or etonogestrel (ETG). These methods fall under Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) Category 1. Women taking NRTIs can generally use the LNG intrauterine device (LNG-IUD) if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2). This is classified as MEC Category 2. Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should generally avoid initiating the LNG-IUD until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease. This is classified as MEC Category 3 for initiation. Women who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed. This is classified as MEC Category 2 for continuation. 2. Non-Nucleoside Reverse Transcriptase Inhibitors (NNRTIs): Women using NNRTIs containing efavirenz or nevirapine can generally use COCs, CICs, contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, NET-EN, and implants (LNG and ETG). These methods are classified as MEC Category 2. DMPA can be used without restriction by women taking efavirenz or nevirapine (MEC Category 1). Women taking NNRTIs can generally use the LNG-IUD if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2) (MEC Category 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should generally avoid initiating the LNG-IUD until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease (MEC Category 3 for initiation). Women who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). 3. Protease Inhibitors (PIs): Women taking protease inhibitors (e.g., ritonavir or ARVs boosted with ritonavir) can generally use COCs, CICs, contraceptive patches and rings, POPs, NET-EN, and implants (LNG and ETG). These methods are classified as MEC Category 2. DMPA can be used without restriction by women taking protease inhibitors (MEC Category 1). Women taking PIs can generally use the LNG-IUD if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2) (MEC Category 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should generally avoid initiating the LNG-IUD until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease (MEC Category 3 for initiation). Women who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). 4. Integrase Inhibitors (e.g., Raltegravir): Women using the integrase inhibitor raltegravir can use all hormonal contraceptive methods without restriction (MEC Category 1). Women taking raltegravir can generally use the LNG-IUD if their HIV clinical disease is asymptomatic or mild (WHO Stage 1 or 2) (MEC Category 2). Women with severe or advanced HIV clinical disease (WHO Stage 3 or 4) should generally avoid initiating the LNG-IUD until their condition improves to asymptomatic or mild disease (MEC Category 3 for initiation). Women who already have an LNG-IUD inserted and later develop severe or advanced HIV clinical disease do not need to have the IUD removed (MEC Category 2 for continuation). Definitions of MEC Categories: Category 1: No restriction for the use of the contraceptive method. Category 2: The advantages of using the method generally outweigh the theoretical or proven risks. Category 3: The theoretical or proven risks usually outweigh the advantages of using the method. Category 4: The method represents an unacceptable health risk if used. These recommendations are based on the WHO’s Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use (5th edition, 2015) and are intended to guide healthcare providers in offering safe and effective contraceptive options for women living with HIV who are on ART.
